issues.display_title: Issue #10: Fix Issue Google Drive Connection Doesn't Work
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

albug — 7:55 PM
One thing that doesn't work is the Google drive connection
On both apps

Google Drive backup (sign-in / connect) fails for the tester on both apps. Since it reproduces on both, the cause is almost certainly server-side OAuth configuration in Google Cloud rather than platform code.

Where it lives

Piece File
Drive service — sign-in, folder, rsync, resumable upload lib/services/drive_backup.dart
Riverpod state + backup loop lib/state/backup_providers.dart
Local mirror of what's on Drive (Hive) lib/data/backup_store.dart
Backup screen (select-all + per-image) lib/views/backup_screen.dart
Per-image entry point lib/views/asset_actions.dart
iOS OAuth client id + URL scheme ios/Runner/Info.plist
Setup notes GOOGLE_DRIVE_SETUP.md

GCP project: silicon-topic-858. Scope: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file (non-sensitive).

Suspected root causes (ranked)

1. OAuth consent screen is still in Testing — affects BOTH apps ⚠️ most likely

GOOGLE_DRIVE_SETUP.md records the consent screen as Testing, which means:

  • Only email addresses explicitly added as test users can sign in at all. Anyone else gets blocked ("app has not completed verification" / access_denied) — this alone would make Drive fail on both Android and iOS for a tester who isn't on the list.
  • Refresh tokens expire after 7 days, so even allow-listed testers get silently kicked out roughly weekly.

The code already has a workaround for the second symptom — DriveBackup._isReauthCanceled retries once on Credential Manager's [16] Account reauth failed — which is a strong hint this is already biting in practice.

Fix: flip the consent screen to Production. Because drive.file is non-sensitive this needs no Google security assessment — only the basic branding/support-email fields.

2. Android OAuth client SHA-1 is stale — affects Android only

The Android OAuth client is registered with only the debug keystore SHA-1:

A9:84:94:7E:83:B8:DC:B0:75:AF:4C:56:10:E4:04:D7:93:84:8A:0F

GOOGLE_DRIVE_SETUP.md justifies that with "the release build currently signs with the debug config too" — that is no longer true. android/app/build.gradle.kts now signs release with the upload keystore from android/key.properties, and Play App Signing re-signs with a third key on top:

signingConfig = if (hasReleaseKeystore) {
    signingConfigs.getByName("release")
} else {
    signingConfigs.getByName("debug")
}

Android's Credential Manager authenticates by package name + SHA-1. Any build not signed with the debug key therefore fails with ApiException: 10 (DEVELOPER_ERROR) — which the app surfaces as the generic "Google sign-in failed. Please try again."

Fix: add both missing SHA-1s to the Android OAuth client:

  • the upload keystore's SHA-1 (keytool -list -v -keystore <upload.jks> -alias <alias>)
  • the Play App Signing SHA-1 from Play Console → Setup → App integrity

3. iOS config — verified consistent, deprioritized

Checked and matching, so probably not the iOS cause:

  • PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = co.360viewer.gothru (note: no "u" — deliberately differs from Android's co.u360viewer.gothru)
  • GIDClientID = ...-ia2vs2csb04sabkku3c5anps8ekkea1u.apps.googleusercontent.com
  • reversed client id present in CFBundleURLSchemes

Still worth confirming the iOS OAuth client in GCP is registered against Team ID W433ZFZCX5 and that bundle id.

4. Errors are unreadable — blocks diagnosis either way

BackupController._message() collapses every non-cancel/non-interrupt GoogleSignInException into one string:

default:
  return 'Google sign-in failed. Please try again.';

The Google status code (10 / 12500 / 16) and description are dropped, so a tester's report can't distinguish SHA-1 mismatch from an unverified-app block from a network failure. That is why this report arrives as "doesn't work" with nothing actionable attached.

Acceptance criteria

  • Reproduce and capture the real error on Android (adb logcat / GoogleSignInException code) and on iOS
  • Add the upload-keystore SHA-1 and the Play App Signing SHA-1 to the Android OAuth client in GCP project silicon-topic-858
  • Verify the iOS OAuth client's bundle id + Team ID, and that the Drive API is enabled on the project
  • Move the OAuth consent screen from Testing to Production (no security assessment needed for drive.file)
  • Surface the underlying Google error code/description in the snackbar (or at minimum log it) instead of the generic "Google sign-in failed"
  • End-to-end verify on a release build from Play (not just a debug build): sign in → GoThru folder created → photo + video upload → rsync skips already-uploaded assets on a second run
  • Verify the same flow on a TestFlight/release iOS build
  • Update GOOGLE_DRIVE_SETUP.md — the "release signs with the debug config" note is now stale, and record the final publishing status

Notes

  • The Testing-mode 7-day expiry means this bug can appear fixed and silently regress a week later. Confirm the fix after Production is live, not before.
  • Uploads consume each user's own 15 GB Drive quota; the Drive API itself is free, so this is not a billing/quota-exhaustion issue on our side.

issues.display_title: Issue #11: Implement Google Drive Sync - Multi-Account, Backup, On Drive & Restore (Front End)
issues.main_description_html:
Front End — Google Drive Sync (multi-account, storage, On Drive & restore)

Build the app-side of Google Drive Sync described in the PRD. Today the app has a single-account, one-way backup (lib/views/backup_screen.dart + lib/services/drive_backup.dart). This task turns it into a full integration: multiple connected accounts, one in use at a time, per-account storage figures, a browsable On Drive view, and download back to device.

PRD: #10 — docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-google-drive-sync-prd.md

Goal: a user can answer is my library backed up, where did it go, and can I get it back? in a couple of taps.

⚠️ Two constraints that shape the whole UI

1. drive.file scope — the app only sees files it created itself.
Every "on Drive" surface means the app's own backup folder, never the user's wider Drive. No folder picker. Importing user-made folders is Phase 2 and out of scope.

2. "Backed up" is per account.
A photo backed up to the personal account shows as not backed up while the work account is in use. That is correct behaviour that reads exactly like a bug — every badge, count, empty state and progress label must name the account it refers to.

Screens & scope

1. Accounts screen (new)

Reached from a Google Drive entry in the gallery menu.

  • List of connected accounts — avatar, email, in use state
  • Per row: storage used of total, plus how much of it is this app's backup folder
  • Per row: number of items backed up to that account
  • Add account action
  • Switch account — single tap; copy must not promise it is always silent (Google may show a sign-in prompt)
  • Disconnect — with confirmation making clear that Drive files are never deleted, only app access is withdrawn
  • Unusable account (password changed / access revoked) stays in the list with a Reconnect prompt and its history intact — never silently removed
  • Storage figures refresh on connect and every time this screen opens
  • Empty state (no accounts connected yet)

2. Backup screen (rework of backup_screen.dart)

  • Header names the destination account (avatar + email)
  • Select all / per-item selection, live selected count + total size
  • Pre-flight free-space check — before upload starts, compare selection size against that account's free space and warn up front if it won't fit
  • Live progress (item n of N, size, percentage)
  • Stop — lets in-flight uploads finish, resumable later
  • Already-uploaded items are visibly skipped, not re-sent
  • Per-item "backed up" badge states which account

3. On Drive screen (new)

  • Lists the current account's backup folder contents, grouped by date, newest first
  • Per item: thumbnail, name, size
  • Per item marker: On this device / Not on this device
  • Items already on the device are not selectable by default (no accidental duplicates)
  • Multi-select of missing items → Download
  • Download progress + Stop, mirroring the backup screen
  • Downloaded items land in the device gallery and appear in the app library (refresh the gallery after)
  • Empty state ("nothing backed up to this account yet")

4. Cross-cutting states

  • Loading / error / offline states for every network-backed surface
  • Re-auth required state → Reconnect flow
  • Surface the real Google error (code + description) instead of a generic "Google sign-in failed" — see the sign-in bug already tracked for this feature
  • Switching accounts re-renders every backup badge/count consistently across gallery, backup and On Drive

Where it lives

Piece File
Drive service — sign-in, folder, rsync, resumable upload lib/services/drive_backup.dart
Riverpod state + backup loop lib/state/backup_providers.dart
Local mirror of what's on Drive (Hive) lib/data/backup_store.dart
Backup screen lib/views/backup_screen.dart
Per-item entry point lib/views/asset_actions.dart
Gallery menu entry lib/views/gallery_screen.dart
Shared UI widgets lib/views/ui.dart

Existing single-account state (backup_providers.dart, backup_store.dart) has to become keyed by account, and the backup folder resolved per account: adopt an existing GoThru folder if present, otherwise create PhotoViewer.

Acceptance criteria

  • Connect two Google accounts; both persist across app restart; exactly one is in use
  • Switching accounts updates backed-up badges, counts and the On Drive list to that account's data
  • Storage used/total/free and app-folder size shown per account and refreshed on open
  • Selecting more than the free space shows the warning before any upload starts
  • Backup progress, Stop and resume work; a second run only uploads what's new
  • On Drive view lists the backup folder grouped by date with correct On this device markers
  • Download restores missing items into the device gallery; they appear in the app library
  • Disconnect removes the account from the list, leaves Drive files untouched, keeps the backup record so reconnecting restores state immediately
  • Revoked account shows Reconnect instead of disappearing
  • Verified on a release build (Android) and a TestFlight build (iOS)

Out of scope (v1)

Importing user-created Drive folders (Phase 2 — needs a restricted scope + CASA security assessment) · automatic/background backup · deletion propagation in either direction · shared/Team Drives · backing up to several accounts at once · renaming or editing Drive files · Google Photos (different service, different permissions)
